clue.text: In a position to provide an example

parts.note: taken as written
a stance is a position or posture someone adopts

explanation.surface: Someone well placed to supply an illustration.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance is a case or illustration of something.

clue.text: One lawgiver accepts origin of poetic lays

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: accepts means the lawgiver's name takes a letter inside it

parts.note: Moses brought the Ten Commandments, so is the biblical lawgiver

indicators.note: origin means the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A lawmaker welcomes the beginnings of verse songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lays' is not poems: it is a verb, as in lays down rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To impose a duty or tax is to lay it on someone.

clue.text: Attendant, an archer, is in place

indicators.note: is in means the archer phrase goes inside the word for place

parts.note: a site is a place
an gives the indefinite article A
William Tell was the legendary Swiss archer

explanation.surface: An archer takes his position as a servant.
explanation.definitionFit: A satellite is a follower or dependant that orbits a more powerful figure.

clue.text: Recital is arranged for a particular object

indicators.note: arranged means the letters are set out in a different order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A concert is organised with a special purpose in mind.
explanation.definitionFit: An article is an individual item or thing.

clue.text: Sang about one among the staff

parts.note: C stands for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: among means the word one is placed inside the word for staff

parts.note: a rod is a staff or stick
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sang about a colleague among the workforce.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staff' suggests employees, but here it is a stick.
explanation.definitionFit: To croon is to sing softly and sentimentally.

clue.text: Wet seafood — Gosh!

parts.note: a clam is a shellfish eaten as seafood
'My!' is an exclamation of surprise, like 'Gosh!'

explanation.surface: A diner exclaims at soggy seafood.
explanation.definitionFit: Clammy means damp and sticky to the touch, so moist.

clue.text: But not necessarily a woman of straw at harvest-time

definitions.text: But not necessarily a woman of straw at harvest-time

parts.words: But not necessarily a woman of straw at harvest-time
parts.note: a figure plaited from cereal stalks at harvest, which may be shaped like a woman but need not be

explanation.surface: A hint that the straw figure need not be female.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a plaited straw figure made from the last sheaf at harvest.

clue.text: In conflict with military commander in a way

parts.note: an aga is a Turkish military commander
taken as written
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: Opposing the general in some manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Against means opposed to or in opposition to.

clue.text: Regicide was blessed if he could say "Amen"!

definitions.text: Regicide was blessed if he could say "Amen"!

parts.words: Regicide was blessed if he could say "Amen"!
parts.note: Shakespeare's Scottish king-killer laments that the word Amen stuck in his throat when he had most need of blessing

explanation.surface: A king-killer longs to pray but cannot.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's thane murders King Duncan and then cannot utter Amen.

clue.text: One who asks little abroad, one US city to go round

parts.note: petit is French for small, a foreign word for little
the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: going round means the city's name is turned to run the other way

parts.note: Reno is a city in Nevada

explanation.surface: A modest traveller seeks little while touring an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' tells you the word for little is foreign, here French; 'to go round' reverses the Nevada city's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A petitioner is someone who makes a formal request or plea.

clue.text: Roguish Frenchman left at the beginning of the month

indicators.note: left means the Frenchman is dropped from where he stands at the start of the month's name

parts.note: March is a month of the year
M is short for Monsieur, a French man's title

explanation.surface: A mischievous Frenchman departs on the first of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'left' is a deletion: take the M from the front of MARCH.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch describes a knowing, playfully mischievous manner.

clue.text: No lack of assurance when off-licence ends in disaster

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things wrecked, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stays cool even when the off-licence ends in calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol to take away.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-confidence is a sure belief in one's own abilities, the opposite of a want of poise.

clue.text: Pay — mine's about to finish

indicators.note: about means the word for mines is turned back to front

parts.note: read as the plural mines, which are pits
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A miner grumbles that his workings are almost exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary, especially a cleric's.

clue.text: Nearly measure up everyone by evening

parts.note: nigh means nearly

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the abbreviation is read from bottom to top

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for feet or foot, a measure of length
all means everyone

explanation.surface: Almost everyone measures up by the evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightfall is dusk, the onset of darkness.

clue.text: Upset by cloth with stains

indicators.note: to upset is to knock over, so these letters are tipped into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a marked tablecloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotchy means covered in patches or marks.

clue.text: Joining in, in search procedure :

indicators.note: the second in means the first one is placed inside the search word

parts.note: combing an area is searching it thoroughly
taken as written

explanation.surface: Volunteers join in a fingertip search.
explanation.definitionFit: Combining means joining things together.

clue.text: Woman in time becomes mean

indicators.note: in means the woman's name goes inside the word for time

parts.note: an age is a long period of time
Vera is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman turns stingy as she grows older.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean in the arithmetic sense is the typical value of a set.

clue.text: Leave state to a large deer …

parts.note: VA is the abbreviation for Virginia, a US state
a moose is the largest kind of deer

explanation.surface: Someone tells a moose to clear off out of the state.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis leads into 17 down, the next deer.
explanation.definitionFit: Vamoose is slang for clear off, depart hurriedly.

clue.text: …another being a Yuletide pathfinder

parts.note: following on from the large deer of 16 down, another deer is the red-nosed one who lights the way for the Christmas sleigh

explanation.surface: A second deer guides the Christmas journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The red-nosed reindeer of the song leads Santa's sleigh through fog.

clue.text: Girl in the swim, back in shape

indicators.note: back means the whole combination is read from end to start
in means the girl's name is placed inside the word for a swim

parts.note: a dip is a swim
Mary is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A girl swimming returns to fitness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the swim' looks like part of the girl's setting, but it is a noun for a dip; 'in' and 'back' then act on the whole, one placed inside and everything reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: A pyramid is a solid geometric figure with triangular faces meeting at a point.

clue.text: Charge a penny before nurse comes in

parts.note: p is the abbreviation for a penny

indicators.note: comes in means the nurse goes inside the word for before

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
a VAD was a volunteer nurse in Britain's Voluntary Aid Detachment

explanation.surface: A fee of a penny is charged before the nurse arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charge' is a verb, to fill or permeate, not a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: To pervade is to spread through and fill, as a room charged with tension.

clue.text: Give voice to a private grudge

indicators.note: giving voice to a word means saying it out loud, so we want a word that sounds like it

parts.note: a ranker is a soldier in the ranks, such as a private

explanation.surface: A soldier airs a long-held grievance.
explanation.definitionFit: Rancour is bitter long-lasting resentment.

clue.text: Turn 'aside' to seek information concerning ship

parts.note: to dig is to probe for facts
re means concerning or about
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A reporter turns away to research a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To digress is to stray from the main subject.

clue.text: Arrived in time for race and was a pace-setter

explanation.surface: A runner arrived punctually and then led the field.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally it means getting to the race in time; idiomatically it means setting the pace or taking the lead.

clue.text: A mere game

explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small lake or pond; it is also a cue game played on a table with pockets.

clue.text: Turn against one

indicators.note: turn tells us to twist these letters round into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to make someone hostile to oneself.
explanation.definitionFit: To antagonise someone is to make them hostile, turning them against you.

clue.text: Hired Henry as a killer

parts.note: let means rented out or hired
Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal

explanation.surface: A man named Henry was hired as an assassin.
explanation.definitionFit: Lethal means deadly, able to cause death.

clue.text: Titles always found in parts of books

indicators.note: found in means the word for always sits inside the word for book parts

parts.note: pages make up books
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: Titles constantly appear in sections of books.
explanation.definitionFit: Peerages are the ranks of nobility such as baron or earl.
